newsitem.title: USA: World's smallest Rembrandt sells for big money.
newsitem.headline: World's smallest Rembrandt sells for big money.

text.p: The world's smallest Rembrandt -- a wallet-sized portrait of an old man -- sold for $2.9 million at Sotheby's on Thursday, and the auctioneers said that, per square inch (cm), it could be the most expensive painting.
The portrait, painted in 1633, was part of a collection of eight Old Master paintings owned by millionaire Saul Steinberg that was being sold.
It measures 4-1/4 inches (10.8 cm) by 2-1/2 inches (6.4 cm), about the length of an average wallet and two-thirds as long as a dollar bill.
The Rembrandt was bought by a private European collector. The entire Steinberg collection sold for $10.9 million.
The pre-sale estimate for the Rembrandt was between $1.5 million and $2 million.
